subject: Chemistry
topic: Solutions, suspensions and colloids — mixed tiers
description: True solutions, suspensions, colloids, Tyndall effect, examples (milk, fog, smoke, gel)

questions.stem: The size of the dispersed particles in a true SOLUTION is typically:

options.option_text: Greater than 1000 nm (settles on standing)
Less than 1 nm (single molecules or ions)
Between 100 nm and 1000 nm (visible cloudiness)
Between 1 nm and 100 nm (typical colloid size)

questions.explanation: True solution — particle size < 1 nm (single molecules / ions). Colloid — 1-100 nm (intermediate). Suspension — > 100 nm (visible particles, settle on standing). Tyndall effect (light scattering) is shown by COLLOIDS, not by true solutions. Distractor 1 = clear suspension range. Distractor 3 = coarse suspension. Distractor 4 = colloid range.

questions.stem: The TYNDALL EFFECT — visible scattering of a beam of light — is shown by:

options.option_text: True solutions of salt or sugar in water
Colloidal systems such as milk and dilute starch
Pure distilled water in a clean glass beaker
Crystals of solid sodium chloride lying still

questions.explanation: Tyndall effect — visible scattering of light by particles in colloidal range (1-100 nm), comparable to wavelength of visible light. Demonstrated when sunlight passes through fog, smoke, or a beam of light through milk diluted in water. True solutions: particles too small to scatter visible light, so the beam passes invisibly. Distractor 4 — solids do not show Tyndall (no dispersion medium).

questions.stem: MILK is best classified as which type of colloid?

options.option_text: Solid in liquid (sol — like paint or muddy water)
Liquid in liquid (emulsion of fat globules in water)
Gas in liquid (foam — like beer head or whipped cream)
Liquid in gas (aerosol — like fog or hairspray mist)

questions.explanation: Milk = an EMULSION — liquid (fat globules) dispersed in another liquid (water). Stabilised by casein protein acting as the emulsifying agent. Distractor 1 (sol) — paint/mud. Distractor 3 (foam) — beer head, whipped cream. Distractor 4 (aerosol) — fog, perfume mist. Other emulsions: butter (water in fat — reverse), mayonnaise (oil in water).

questions.stem: FOG is a colloidal system. The dispersed phase is _____ and the dispersion medium is _____.

options.option_text: Solid in gas (smoke-like behaviour)
Liquid in gas (fine water droplets in air)
Gas in liquid (bubbles within a fluid)
Liquid in solid (gel-like trapped water)

questions.explanation: Fog / mist / cloud — tiny LIQUID water droplets dispersed in GAS (air). This is called an AEROSOL. Smoke — solid particles in gas (different aerosol). Foam — gas in liquid. Gel — liquid in solid (e.g. jelly, agar). Smog (smoke + fog) — mixed solid + liquid in gas; characteristic of polluted urban areas in winter (Delhi smog).

questions.stem: Which of the following is a TRUE SOLUTION (NOT a colloid or suspension)?

options.option_text: Muddy river water held in a glass jar
Salt fully dissolved in clean tap water
Whole milk standing on a kitchen table
Smoke rising from a freshly extinguished candle

questions.explanation: Salt-in-water — true solution (Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions dispersed at molecular level). Particle size < 1 nm; transparent; no Tyndall effect; passes through filter paper without residue. Distractor 1 — coarse suspension (settles on standing). Distractor 3 — colloid (emulsion). Distractor 4 — aerosol colloid (solid particles in gas).

questions.stem: Brownian motion of colloidal particles can be observed under a microscope. The motion is caused by:

options.option_text: Convection currents in the surrounding liquid
Random collisions with surrounding solvent molecules
Electrostatic repulsion between dispersed particles
Gravity pulling the particles toward the bottom

questions.explanation: Brownian motion — irregular zig-zag motion of colloidal particles caused by unequal random collisions with surrounding solvent molecules at any moment. Discovered by Robert Brown (1827) watching pollen grains in water. Einstein's 1905 paper on Brownian motion provided the first quantitative evidence for the existence of atoms — won him recognition. Distractor 1 — convection is bulk flow, not the random microscopic motion. Distractor 3 — repulsion would not produce random zig-zag. Distractor 4 — gravity gives a one-way drift, not zig-zag.

questions.stem: An EMULSIFYING agent like soap added to oil + water mixture works by:

options.option_text: Dissolving the oil completely into the water phase
Coating each droplet so they cannot rejoin one another
Heating the mixture so that the oil layer evaporates
Filtering out the oil through extremely fine pores

questions.explanation: An emulsifier (soap, lecithin in egg yolk, casein in milk) has both hydrophilic and hydrophobic parts. The hydrophobic tail embeds in the oil droplet; the hydrophilic head faces water → forms a stable shell around each oil droplet, preventing coalescence. This is how soap cleans grease: surrounds + emulsifies the grease so water can wash it away. Distractor 1 — oil does not actually dissolve in water; it is dispersed. Distractor 3 — heating doesn't emulsify. Distractor 4 — filtering doesn't apply to liquid-liquid mixtures.
